title: 'Huh?' is a word shaped by repair, not a grunt and not proof of one innate form
body: Dingemanse, Torreira, and Enfield (2013) compared a short questioning interjection used to initiate repair, in naturally occurring conversation in ten languages. They argue two things: that this item is universal, in the sense that a short questioning interjection with the function of other-initiation of repair is likely in every spoken language and is more similar across languages than chance would produce; and that it is a word, a conventional form that has to be learned, not a grunt or an emotional cry. Their account of the similarity is convergent cultural evolution under a shared interactional pressure, not an innate lexical item. Do not treat the English spelling 'huh' as a token every language uses. Do not treat an open repair initiator as a feeling. It means the previous turn was not received.

sources.title: Is 'Huh?' a universal word? Conversational infrastructure and the convergent evolution of linguistic items
sources.author: Mark Dingemanse, Francisco Torreira, and N. J. Enfield
